item.title: Mini Crackme: Rolling Checksum (Windows x64)
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64. check takes a pointer to a null-terminated ASCII string in rcx and returns al=1 if it's the password.
check: mov r8, rcx xor eax, eax xor edx, edx .loop: movzx ecx, byte ptr [r8+rdx] test ecx, ecx je .done rol eax, 1 add eax, ecx inc edx jmp .loop .done: cmp eax, 0x20F sete al ret
Find an ASCII password that makes check return 1.
Answer: KEY
Explanation: Each iteration computes acc = rol(acc,1) + byte, a rolling-hash accumulator. Since acc stays small, bit 31 is always 0, so rol eax,1 behaves like acc*2. For "KEY": ((75*2+69)*2+89) = 527 = 0x20F, which matches the target, so cmp/sete sets al=1.
